t: The treatise treats war as a costly and destructive last resort and teaches how to keep it brief, contained and cheap, with a stress on diplomacy, economic principles and intelligence.

Its author is disputed: tradition names Sun Tzu of the 6th century BCE, while scholars have doubted that he existed, and the 1972 Yinqueshan slips showed that two related texts bore the name of Master Sun.
For almost 1,500 years it was the lead text of an anthology formalised in 1080 as the Seven Military Classics, and it has been read by military and political leaders in East Asia and the West.
dyk: The earliest known commentary on the text, written by a strategist and warlord in the early 3rd century, comes with a preface admitting that he edited the book and removed certain passages; how much he changed has never been clear.
ev: Sun Tzu, the traditional author, is said to have lived in this century
The earlier text of The Art of War is now generally accepted as completed between 500 and 430 BCE
Two Han tombs near Linyi in Shandong are sealed between 134 and 118 BCE with bamboo slips that include the Sun Tzu text
A strategist and warlord writes the earliest known commentary and edits the text
Emperor Shenzong of Song formalises the Seven Military Classics, with The Art of War at their head
The French Jesuit Jean Joseph Marie Amiot produces the first translation into a European language
Lionel Giles publishes the first annotated English translation
The Yinqueshan Han slips are discovered in the two tombs near Linyi

f.made: Attributed by tradition to the strategist Sun Tzu (Sun Wu) of the state of Qi, said to have served King Helü of Wu; the earlier text was probably completed between 500 and 430 BCE
f.form: A Chinese military treatise in 13 chapters (piān), counted as one zhuàn, written on bamboo slips in its earliest surviving copies
f.where: Read in many editions and translations; the Yinqueshan Han slips, with an early copy of the text, were found in two tombs near Linyi in Shandong
f.known: War as a costly last resort; keeping war brief and cheap; diplomacy and economy in strategy; espionage and intelligence; the Seven Military Classics; readers from Takeda Shingen to Mao Zedong and Võ Nguyên Giáp
